final_codebook.domain: Subtraction of fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Match denominators
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite fractional parts as equivalent fractions before subtraction when denominators differ.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution explicitly finds an LCD or other common denominator.
Tag when one or both fractions are converted to equivalent fractions so the denominators match before subtraction.
Tag in pure-fraction or mixed-number items when unlike fractional parts are reconciled before subtracting.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no equivalent-fraction conversion is performed.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator; that is operand normalization.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping or post-subtraction simplification.

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or mixed number into a subtraction-ready form, such as adding a 0-fraction part or converting an improper fractional part to a standard mixed number.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0 over a chosen denominator.
Tag when a mixed number with an improper fraction part is normalized to an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when the rewrite prepares the quantities for later whole-part and fraction-part subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag ordinary common-denominator conversion between existing fractions; that is denominator matching.
Do not tag borrowing from the whole part after subtraction has begun.
Do not tag direct subtraction when the quantities are already in subtraction-ready form.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out the subtraction once forms are aligned by subtracting like-denominator fractions and/or subtracting the whole-number and fractional parts separately.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a common denominator.
Tag when whole parts and fraction parts of mixed numbers are subtracted as separate components.
Tag when the solution performs the main subtraction after any needed normalization or denominator matching, including a temporary negative fractional part before borrowing.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag the step that creates common denominators or rewrites operands into subtraction-ready form.
Do not tag the borrowing/regrouping step itself.
Do not tag final simplification or recombination unless subtraction is explicitly performed in that step.

skills.name: Borrow in subtraction
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units and adjust the whole part when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to subtract.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution borrows 1 from the whole part and converts it to denominator-over-denominator fractional units.
Tag when a negative fractional difference is corrected by regrouping across whole and fraction parts.
Tag in mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction subtraction requiring regrouping.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when subtraction is completed without regrouping.
Do not tag initial rewriting of a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator.
Do not tag the subsequent subtraction after borrowing unless the step itself explicitly performs the regrouping.

skills.name: Finalize result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms when needed and express it in the appropriate final form as a fraction, mixed number, integer, or 0.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is simplified, such as reducing 2/10 to 1/5 or converting 0 over a denominator to 0.
Tag when separate whole and fractional results are combined into a single final mixed number, fraction, or integer.
Tag when a step both simplifies and recombines the result, or when either of those finalization actions is shown explicitly.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag denominator matching, operand normalization, or borrowing.
Do not tag intermediate subtraction steps that do not simplify or present the final expressed result.
Do not tag answers already in final form unless the solution explicitly performs or states the simplification/combination step.

decisions.reasoning: This skill had 3/3 consensus and a clear, independently testable boundary distinct from normalization, subtraction, borrowing, and simplification.

decisions.details: Renamed C02 from 'Normalize mixed form' to S02 'Normalize operands'
decisions.reasoning: The broader name better covers both whole-number rewrites and mixed-number normalization while preserving the 3/3 consensus concept.

decisions.details: Merged C03 + C04 + C05 into S03
decisions.reasoning: Whole-part subtraction and like-denominator fraction subtraction are not independently represented across the item set in a diagnostically useful way; A and C already treat them as one execution skill, while B's split is a granularity difference rather than a distinct underlying process. Merging improves minimality and identifiability.
This skill had 3/3 consensus and is a distinct cognitive operation: regrouping across whole and fractional parts when direct subtraction is not possible.

decisions.details: Merged C07 + C08 + C09 into S05
decisions.reasoning: Simplification and final expression are separated in A/C but combined in B, and in the dossiers they frequently occur as adjacent end-of-solution actions with limited independent coverage. A single finalization skill better satisfies minimality while still covering all observed end-state operations.

decisions.details: Removed standalone candidates C03 and C04 after consolidation into S03
decisions.reasoning: Keeping them separate would over-fragment the execution phase and reduce annotation consistency because many steps in the dossiers subtract whole and fraction parts within the same solution move.

decisions.details: Removed standalone candidates C07, C08, and C09 after consolidation into S05
decisions.reasoning: A unified finalization skill avoids ambiguous tagging between simplification-only, composition-only, and combined end steps, improving clarity of boundaries for annotators.

summary: The final codebook consolidates the aligned candidates into 5 skills: denominator matching, operand normalization, aligned subtraction, borrowing/regrouping, and result finalization. Strong-consensus skills were preserved, while low-consensus granularity splits were merged when they did not add enough independent diagnostic value across the item set. The main consolidation choices were to combine whole-part and fraction-part subtraction into one execution skill and to combine simplification with final expression into one end-of-solution skill.
